name: request-response
description: Windowed RPC round trips over one link - the network's most common interactive pattern (page fetches, queries, telemetry): each request a varied size, each naming a varied response size it wants back, the handler answering through the engine-gated allow list. Latency is the product; requests per second the capacity.
conformance: sent == delivered + timeouts + raced; every response carries exactly the byte count its request named. Known reference asymmetry: RNS 1.3.5 registers a pending request AFTER sending it (Link.py request->RequestReceipt), so a responder answering inside that gap races the match and the response drops silently; sub-MDU requests then have no response timeout, so each raced slot is a permanent zombie. Against a sub-millisecond responder this fires ~1 in 15-20k and ends the run when the window is exhausted - judge reference-initiator rows by the per-second settle histogram.
